classification.difficultyReason: Combine changing annual multipliers, convert the product to a percentage increase, and explain why reversing their order preserves the result.

content.prompt: One six-year loan attracts compound interest calculated at $2\%$, $4\%$, $6\%$, $8\%$, $10\%$ and $12\%$ in successive years. Another six-year loan attracts compound interest calculated at $12\%$, $10\%$, $8\%$, $6\%$, $4\%$ and $2\%$ in successive years. Find the total percentage increase in money owing in both cases, correct to 2 decimal places, compare the two results, and explain what has happened.

answer.short:
$49.61\%$ for both loans.

Reversing the order of the annual multipliers does not change their product.
answer.worked:
For the first loan:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.02\times1.04\times1.06\times1.08\times1.10\times1.12\\\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.49614553088\end{aligned}$$
For the second loan:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.12\times1.10\times1.08\times1.06\times1.04\times1.02\\\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.49614553088\end{aligned}$$
Thus, for each loan:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage increase}&=(1.49614553088-1)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx49.61\%\end{aligned}$$
Both loans have the same percentage increase because multiplication is commutative: changing the order of the annual multipliers does not change their product.
